awarding_org: Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters
funding_share_basis: The purse is USD 1,000,000 per field (plus gold medal and scroll). The Kavli Foundation (Los Angeles, US) has supplied 100% of the purse and medals since the first award in 2008, satisfying the >50% rule at both origin and today. The Norwegian Ministry of Education and Research pays only administration: it funds the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters and hosts the prize banquet, which is operations money and excluded from the purse test. No change of funder at any point.
money_note: USD 1,000,000 per field, paid in full by The Kavli Foundation since the prize's first award in 2008 and unchanged through the 2026 cycle.
status_note: Continuity is clean: awarded biennially in even years since 2008 under the same name, most recently in 2026. No rename, merger, suspension, or missed cycle.
evidence_quote: The Kavli Foundation "provides the award money and gold medals to The Kavli Prize Laureates"; the Norwegian Ministry of Education and Research "hosts The Kavli Prize Banquet and provides funding to The Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters."
judgment_reason: The official site splits the roles: the US Kavli Foundation pays the purse while the Norwegian Ministry of Education and Research funds the Academy's administration and banquet. Applying the >50%-of-purse rule, the funder is the Kavli Foundation (Philanthropy, United States) in both states; a coder counting the state's operational subsidy could instead code Mixed or Government/Norway. The awarding body is coded Society under the national-academy rule despite its state support.
